subject: POC metrics & evaluation roadmap — BlueHorizon Analytics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@bluehorizon.com>, Erin Moss <erin.moss@bluehorizon.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC metrics & evaluation roadmap — BlueHorizon Analytics

Hi Samir / Erin,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the recommendation engine use case. As discussed, I pulled together a concise POC roadmap and the candidate success metrics so we can confirm alignment before we spin up dedicated capacity. High-level ask: please review the success criteria below and reply with any edits by EOD Thurs so we can lock the scope and schedule.

POC goal (4 weeks): validate that Redwood inference can meet BlueHorizon’s latency, throughput, and quality targets on the real query mix while providing predictable cost/unit.

Proposed success criteria (PASS/FAIL):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 350 ms for 256-512 token prompts (measured at service boundary, cold start excluded).
- Throughput: sustained throughput of 120 requests/minute with tail-latency SLA <= 500 ms under synthetic concurrency profile matching BH peak traffic.
- Cost: projected cost/token <= $0.0009 for the evaluated workload and model quantization profile (target is conservative to compare to your current unit economics).
- Quality: top-line quality acceptance via n=500 evaluation prompts (sample attached) with at least 85% pass rate on rubric: intent accuracy, factuality, and hallucination tolerance (we’ll provide rubric and annotation instructions).

Evaluation plan / instrumentation:
- Data: BH provides a 3k sample of anonymized queries + ground-truth responses (we’ve requested the sample attached: bh_poc_data_sample.csv).
- Metrics capture: Redwood will enable request-level tracing and token-level cost reporting; BH will get a dashboard link and raw CSV exports weekly.
- Test harness: Redwood test harness will replay sampled traffic and run the n=500 evaluation suite (can be run in-house or we can ship evaluation artifacts).

Timeline (target):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize sample & sign SOW.
- Week 1: infra & model selection, baseline runs.
- Week 2: focused tuning (batching, KV cache settings, quantization candidate).
- Week 3: full replay & quality evaluation.
- Week 4: final report + cost/ops recommendations.

Owners / next steps:
- BlueHorizon: confirm dataset ownership and provide sample + point of contact for redaction (Owner: Samir).
- Redwood: spin up dedicated POC pool, share SOW draft, and provide weekly dashboard (Owner: Camila + Rishi).
- Legal/procurement: exchange SOW and finalize procurement timeline (Owner: Erin).

Attachments: bh_poc_data_sample.csv (sample rows), redwood_poc_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook + eval rubric), SOW_BlueHorizon_Draft.docx (draft scope & commercials).

Please reply with any edits to the metrics or timeline — if this looks good I’ll send the SOW for signature and propose a start week the week of Mar 8.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Camila —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side before we lock: 
1) Latency baseline: our current 95th is ~420 ms on your baseline model under real traffic. P95 <= 350 ms would be a meaningful win — can Redwood demonstrate that on our sample without aggressive quantization that might hurt quality?
2) Quality rubric: the 85% pass threshold is reasonable, but can you share the rubric and an example annotated response so our product manager sees the grading?
3) Security: we’ll need confirmation that the POC data will only be used for this evaluation and confirm retention period (we typically ask 30 days post-project).

Also tagging Erin for procurement timelines — we’re shooting to get a POC signed by Mar 12.

Thanks,
Samir Gupta
Sr. Product Manager, BlueHorizon Analytics
samir.g@bluehorizon.com

Samir — quick answers inline and a couple of operational notes.

> 1) Latency baseline: our current 95th is ~420 ms on your baseline model under real traffic. P95 <= 350 ms would be a meaningful win — can Redwood demonstrate that on our sample without aggressive quantization that might hurt quality?

Yes — we plan to test three model configurations during Week 1–2:
- baseline FP16 (no quantization) — should match current.
- mixed-int8 (light quant) — expected 15–25% latency reduction with minimal quality deviation.
- aggressive quantized variant (int8+cache tuning) — best latency but we’ll validate quality tradeoffs.

We will report per-config quality metrics so you can decide on the acceptable cost/latency tradeoff.

> 2) Quality rubric: the 85% pass threshold is reasonable, but can you share the rubric and an example annotated response so our product manager sees the grading?

Attached in the playbook (redwood_poc_playbook_v1.pdf) is the rubric and two annotated examples. If you want, we can run a 30-min annotation alignment session with your PM during Week 0.

> 3) Security: we’ll need confirmation that the POC data will only be used for this evaluation and confirm retention period (we typically ask 30 days post-project).

Confirmed — we’ll scope a 30 day retention window in the SOW and redact logs on request. RACI: Camila will coordinate SOW edits with Legal; I’ll ensure the config flags for log retention are set on the POC cluster.

Operational notes:
- We’ll provide an instrumentation guide (tracing + token-cost headers) and a sandbox dashboard link for you to monitor during the run.
- We recommend a mid-week check-in during Week 2 for tuning decisions (I can schedule).

Laura — quick ask: can we reserve a small GPU pool the week of Mar 8 (2x A100-equivalent) while the SOW is finalized?

-Rishi
